title: Canary Driver Upgrade Orchestration + Terraform snippets
content:
Summary:
This is a working draft for orchestrating GPU driver upgrades in Redwood private deployments (VPC/on-prem). Focus is on a safe canary flow that integrates Terraform-managed node pools, in-cluster validation tests, and an automated rollback path. Document includes operational choreography, Terraform module guidance, a short compatibility matrix excerpt, validation commands, and metrics to watch during upgrades.

Goals:
- Perform driver/CUDA/NCCL upgrades with minimal application disruption.
- Provide a Terraform-centric workflow so infra teams can version and roll node pools declaratively.
- Capture deterministic smoke tests and KPIs to approve canary->rollout progression.
- Support multi-vendor clusters (NVIDIA A100, H100; AMD MI250 experimental) and mixed nodepools.

Scope / Assumptions:
- Cluster(s) are managed with k8s >=1.24 and kubelet flag management via node taints/labels.
- GPU nodes are provisioned with node pools controlled by Terraform modules.
- We control SSH access and can run smoke tests against nodes directly.
- Drivers are NVIDIA or NV driver variants; AMD support is separated and out-of-scope for this doc.

High-level canary flow (safe-by-default):
1) Prepare: build AMI/node-image containing new driver package + bootstrap script. Publish artifact with semver (e.g., image:gdriver-525.85-20260210).
2) Terraform create: create a small canary nodepool (1-3 nodes) with image=canary. Use lifecycle.prevent_destroy=false for ephemeral pools.
3) Drain and label: schedule canary jobs by adding label gpu-upgrade=canary. Do not route production traffic.
4) Run validation suite: device probe, CUDA smoke, NCCL ring test, regression prompt latency test against a pinned model.
5) Observe metrics for N minutes (suggest 30m baseline, 2h extended). If failure -> roll back by replacing canary nodes with previous image or scale-to-zero and destroy nodepool.
6) Gradual rollout: increase nodepool sizes and/or create new nodepools with image tag rolled forward.
7) Post-mortem & promote images to stable.

Terraform module notes and snippets:
- Module design: nodepool module should accept image_id, driver_version, taints, labels, and drain_timeout. Keep image_id separate from driver_version to avoid implicit changes.
- Use lifecycle.ignore_changes = ["metadata[0].annotations"] for fields mutated by cluster-autoscaler.
- Add plan-time checks (pre-commit hook or CI step) that fail if the plan contains both scale_down and replace actions across multiple pools unless flagged.

Example variables (module interface):
- variable "image_id" { type = string }
- variable "gpu_driver_version" { type = string }
- variable "canary" { type = bool, default = false }
- variable "node_labels" { type = map(string) }

Example Terraform usage (snippet):
module "gpu_nodepool_canary" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo.redwood.ai/infra/terraform-modules.git//nodepool"
  image_id = var.canary_image_id
  gpu_driver_version = "525.85"
  canary = true
  node_labels = { "gpu-upgrade" = "canary" }
}

Plan guard examples (CI):
- Reject plans that change more than N nodes in a single PR.
- Enforce explicit manual approval if any nodepool replacement count > 3.

Compatibility matrix excerpt (short, curated):
- k8s 1.24 | NVIDIA driver 520.x | CUDA 11.7 | NCCL 2.14 | Notes: stable on A100; watch kernel module load latency.
- k8s 1.25 | NVIDIA driver 525.x | CUDA 12.0 | NCCL 2.16 | Notes: recommended for H100; requires newer nvidia-container-runtime 3+.
- k8s 1.26 | NVIDIA driver 535.x | CUDA 12.1 | NCCL 2.17 | Notes: improved peer-to-peer on mixed vGPU setups.
- k8s 1.23 | NVIDIA driver 470.x | CUDA 11.4 | NCCL 2.10 | Notes: legacy, only for older A100 SKUs; avoid on nodes with updated kernel > 5.15.

Validation tests (run on canary nodes and from cluster):
- Driver probe: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv
- CUDA compile smoke: compile and run vector-add sample via nvcc or container run of official CUDA samples.
- NCCL ring test: run nccl-tests all-reduce with replica count matching expected pod distribution.
- Container runtime check: docker/CRI logs for failing devices or permission denials.
- ML inference regression: run a small batch (10 requests) against canary endpoints, track latency and token-level diffs.

Sample shell smoke-check (to run on node):
# probe
command: nvidia-smi -q | egrep "Driver Version|CUDA Version|GPU Current Temp"
# cuda sample run
docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.0-base nvidia-smi
# nccl quick test (inside cluster job):
# launcher: run nccl-tests/all_reduce for 2 ranks and verify no process hangs

Observable KPIs for go/no-go:
- GPU device readiness (k8s node status + device-plugin healthy) must be 100% for canary nodes.
- p90 inference latency change < +10% vs baseline.
- Token error rate from model outputs unchanged within tolerance.
- NCCL all-reduce throughput within -15% of baseline for target batch sizes.
- No OOMs, no kernel module panics in dmesg.

Failure modes and rollback strategies:
- Failure: device-plugin crash loop -> rollback by destroying canary nodepool and re-creating previous image pool.
- Failure: slow nvlink / interconnect throughput -> label affected nodes and exclude from service, schedule remediation, escalate to HW vendor.
- Failure: application-level regressions -> scale canary down to 0, destroy nodepool, pin stable image.
- Automated rollback: CI watchdog that watches health signals for 15m post-upgrade and triggers terraform apply of previous image when thresholds crossed.

Operational runbook checklist (short):
- [ ] Build and publish canary image with driver and kubelet flags.
- [ ] Create canary nodepool via Terraform in staging, run tests.
- [ ] Run smoke test suite and collect baselines.
- [ ] Approve and apply canary to prod small pool.
- [ ] Observe metrics; if green, ramp to 25% cluster capacity.
- [ ] After 24-48h without regressions, promote image to stable.

Open questions / next steps:
- Automation: add a controller that can orchestrate nodepool replacement and run the validation suite end-to-end (PoC tracked in RDW-1452).
- AMD path: define separate module and lower-risk canary sizing.
- Telemetry: capture NVML counters and NCCL perf counters in Prometheus for precise rollback thresholds.

Action items:
- Priya: add Terraform plan guard to infra CI by 2026-02-28.
- Diego: implement nccl-tests job template and add to canary validation suite.
- Lars: prototype a controller that runs tests and gates Terraform apply (PoC RDW-1452).

Notes to self: keep canary image tags small and immutable; prefer creating new nodepools rather than in-place driver replacement on long-lived nodes. Document is intentionally lightweight and operational — expect iteration after first two upgrades.
